contradictions: PROCESS-EXIT DETECTION, opposite defaults. multi-instance M12 says NEVER hold a process handle on RobloxPlayerBeta (Hyperion tripped on a held handle in 2023) and poll the process list, so no exit code is available; tauri-crates T16 recommends the opposite: OpenProcess(PROCESS_SYNCHRONIZE|PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION)+WaitForSingleObject instead of polling. Reconcile: the Hyperion evidence is 2023 and about full-access handles; M12 itself allows a limited-rights waitable handle behind a setting. Default to (PID, create_time) polling; make the waitable handle an opt-in.

browserTrackerId: STABLE-per-account vs UNIQUE-per-launch. auth-launch A21 design says keep a stable browserTrackerId per account (to look like the website, which reuses one id); multi-instance M10 design says generate a unique browsertrackerid per launch so each client's log line ('web launch, websiteBTId is <id>') maps back to one account. These are mutually exclusive. Unique-per-launch should win: it is the only reliable log->account binding, the client honours whatever the URI carries, and website id-reuse is irrelevant for a native launcher.

PRIVATE-SERVER LAUNCH PATH disagrees with itself inside links-private. The L2 finding and its design_implications say privateServerInviteData exposes only status/universeId/linkCode and tell you to map universeId->rootPlaceId via games?universeIds; the L2 verify and 'missed' refute that - placeId, ownerUserId and privateServerId are all present and linkCode is a string. A design built from the finding does an unnecessary extra lookup. Use placeId directly (it equals rootPlaceId, confirmed live), universe lookup only as a fallback.

linkCode VALIDATION conflates two different tokens. auth-launch A21 design validates 'linkCode' as ^[0-9]+$, but there are two distinct codes: the private-server privateServerLinkCode (digits-only, RoSeal ^\d+$, 25-32 digits) and the share-link 'code' (alphanumeric hex, links-private L16 ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$). Applying ^[0-9]+$ to a share code wrongly rejects it; auth-launch verify A21 further muddies this by citing pealz1 'letters and digits' for the private-server code, contradicting links-private's digits-only. Settle on: privateServerLinkCode=digits, share code=alphanumeric, as separate validators.

CSRF enforcement on apis.roblox.com is PER-SERVICE, not uniform, so a single app-wide assumption is wrong. account-info A11: apis.roblox.com get-profiles returns 200 with no CSRF token; links-private L1: apis.roblox.com sharelinks resolve-link returns 403 'XSRF token invalid' with no token; auth-launch A1-verify: friends.roblox.com and apis run the CSRF check BEFORE the auth check. The HTTP layer must do retry-once-on-403-with-x-csrf-token generically per endpoint, never assume a host is exempt.

CSRF-TOKEN LIFETIME: the auth-launch A2 finding as written ('per session, needs no TTL') contradicts its own verify, which observed the guest token rotate within tens of minutes and the old value rejected with 403+new-token. Any design that treats a cached CSRF token as durable (e.g. priming once before a bulk launch) will break mid-run; always retry once on 403 and re-read the header.
outdated_spec_assumptions: 'multi-instance via singleton mutex': the mutex-only method (holding ROBLOX_singletonMutex, the old RAM/Bloxstrap way) STOPPED working ~Jul-Aug 2025 (multi-instance M3). You must pre-create a MUTEX named exactly ROBLOX_singletonEvent - case-sensitive, 'ROBLOX_SingletonEvent' does NOT collide (M3 verify) - with no namespace prefix, owned on a long-lived thread. A tray '--launch-to-tray' process may already hold the name before RoALT starts (M5), in which case CreateMutexW fails and a stock launch would just replace the tray process.

The vault spec omits COOKIE ROTATION. .ROBLOSECURITY now rotates via a Set-Cookie header on arbitrary API responses on a cadence of hours-to-days (auth-launch A10), and formats change without notice from May 2026. The vault must treat the cookie as an opaque string (no format regex, no length cap) and atomically persist any Set-Cookie '.ROBLOSECURITY=' from every host before returning, plus periodically 'touch' idle accounts so they pick up rotations inside the months-long grace window. A static stored cookie silently dies.

The 'multi-instance' + 'bulk launch' spec omits the SHARED LOCAL-STATE hazard. All clients share %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\LocalStorage\RobloxCookies.dat and appStorage.json (multi-instance M6). Concurrent/bulk launches cross-contaminate identity: wrong-account name over a CAPTCHA, teleport error 773/512, and observed account locks during an unprotected Oct-2026 bulk launch. Needs an optional 'shared-login protection' (open both files with share-mode 0 while Roblox is closed, released when the last client exits) and a user warning. Also note that even a SINGLE launch rewrites the shared store, so launching account B replaces whatever the user's normal desktop Roblox app was logged into.

'account info panel' implicitly showing Premium is outdated. Premium stopped selling Apr 2026 and the Premium profile badge ended 2026-05-30 (account-info A10); Roblox Plus replaced it. Subscription status should come from apis.roblox.com user-profile-api get-profiles field 'hasRobloxSubscription' (A11), with premiumfeatures validate-membership (legacy, 'planned for deprecation on 4/30') only as a best-effort fallback. Hide the badge rather than error when either source fails.

The auth-ticket mental model (single POST, no body, the old RAM way) is a confirmed mismatch. The site now does GET https://auth.roblox.com/v1/client-assertion/ then POST /v1/authentication-ticket/ with Content-Type application/json and body = the assertion JSON or {}, reading the ticket from the rbx-authentication-ticket RESPONSE header, fetched immediately before each launch and never cached (auth-launch A4/A13). CSRF must come from the request itself (send real POST, on 403 store x-csrf-token and retry once) - NEVER prime it via /v2/logout, which destroys the session if a valid token is attached.

'embedded login webview cookie capture' is fine for READING (Tauri cookies_for_url on a worker thread, never in a sync command/event handler or it deadlocks on Windows - tauri T2). But cookie INJECTION for 'open roblox.com as account X' must NOT use Tauri set_cookie: it strips the leading dot from the Domain ('.roblox.com'->'roblox.com'), producing a host-only cookie that subdomains never receive, and it is fire-and-forget (errors only log::error!) - tauri T3. Inject via raw ICoreWebView2CookieManager.CreateCookie with Domain '.roblox.com', HttpOnly, Secure (T4). Also, Enhanced Protection can force passkeys for some accounts, so only the real webview login works - a native user/pass path would fail; manual-paste is the fallback.

'server browser' assumes open access. The unauthenticated server list is 3 requests/min per route per IP on a fixed wall-clock-minute window (servers-games S3), and even 400-responses consume quota; a logged-in-only server-list restriction has been announced by staff (not yet enforced, S4), and Recommended/BestLatency/Friend sorts already require a cookie. The browser must throttle per route from the x-ratelimit-* headers (reset to :00, not retry-after:5) and use the selected account's cookie.

'same-server mode' built on presence/following is fragile. Presence returns game fields only to an authenticated viewer the target's privacy allows, and is laggy (servers-games D1/D2). The robust pattern (MultiAlt) is to pick ONE jobId from the public server list BEFORE launching anyone (playing+N<=maxPlayers), then launch every account with PlaceLauncher RequestGameJob&gameId=<jobId>. 'Follow account #1' (RequestFollowUser) only works if account #1's join-privacy permits the alts, so it should be an option, not the default.

DPAPI-for-everything breaks 'encrypted backup import/export'. DPAPI (CryptProtectData, tauri T11) is bound to the current user AND machine, so a DPAPI-sealed vault cannot be restored on another machine or user account. Portable backups MUST use the master-password path (Argon2id at ~64MiB/t=3 -> AES-256-GCM, random 96-bit nonce per message; tauri T12 - note aes-gcm 0.11 removed the OsRng generate APIs), never DPAPI. Also keep cookie values Rust-side: never send them across IPC to the webview UI panel.

Log-based auto-rejoin/instance-tracking omits a secret-handling requirement: the auth ticket (gameinfo:<ticket>) is written in PLAINTEXT to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\logs (the UpdateController 'Update thread: start' line and the installer -relaunch line) and to the process command line (multi-instance missed). Any log reading, command-line reading, or diagnostics export MUST redact gameinfo:. Also clear WebView2 override env vars (WEBVIEW2_USER_DATA_FOLDER etc.) at startup, or they silently collapse every per-account login UDF into one and leak cookies between accounts (tauri missed).

resolved_gaps.question: For a type=Server share link, what is the full privateServerInviteData schema, is linkCode a string, and do we need a universeId->rootPlaceId lookup before launching?
resolved_gaps.answer: Full payload: {status:'Invalid'|'Valid'|'Expired', ownerUserId:number, universeId:number, privateServerId:number, linkCode:string, placeId:number}. linkCode IS a string (treat it as a bearer credential; redact in logs). placeId is present and equals the universe rootPlaceId - confirmed live today: apis.roblox.com/universes/v1/places/18980972074/universe -> {universeId:6430220996}, and games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds=6430220996 -> rootPlaceId 18980972074. So launch RequestPrivateGame with placeId (from the payload) + linkCode, accessCode empty; the games?universeIds lookup is only a FALLBACK for when placeId is absent. This refutes the links-private L2 finding (which claimed only status/universeId/linkCode exist) and overrides its design_implications.
sources: links-private L2 verify (RoSeal sharelinks.ts, Froststrap GameJoin.cs)

resolved_gaps.question: Which named kernel object does the current RobloxPlayerBeta use as its singleton, and does pre-creating it work? (tauri-crates T15 left this unverified.)
resolved_gaps.answer: Resolved by the dedicated multi-instance topic, which the tauri-crates author did not have. Binary scan of client 0.744 (multi-instance M1): both ROBLOX_singletonEvent and ROBLOX_singletonMutex appear as ASCII strings in RobloxPlayerBeta.exe with NO Local\/Global\ prefix. The EVENT is what drives the single-instance replacement (M2 logs); pre-creating a MUTEX named exactly ROBLOX_singletonEvent (case-sensitive) blocks a new client because the client's CreateEvent on that name then fails with a type clash (M3). Mutex-only (ROBLOX_singletonMutex) no longer prevents replacement. So tauri-crates' CreateMutexW/CreateEventW design should target ROBLOX_singletonEvent specifically.
sources: multi-instance M1/M2/M3 (local static scan + %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox logs, client 0.744)

resolved_gaps.question: What are the v2 server-list orderBy (ServerListSortOption) enum values, and should we send ints or strings? (servers-games S5 open question.)
resolved_gaps.answer: Send the STRING names - OccupancyDesc, OccupancyAsc, Recommended, BestLatency are all confirmed working in ServerList.js and live. Guest probes map the ints as: 0=default (occupancy-desc), 1 and 2 = Recommended/BestLatency (both return 400 'Guest users are not allowed.' unauthenticated, i.e. cookie-only), 3=OccupancyDesc, 4=OccupancyAsc. The website itself sends sortOrder=Desc&excludeFullGames=true&orderBy=Recommended (authed) or OccupancyDesc (guest). v2 ignores sortOrder for ordering.

resolved_gaps.question: If RoALT spawns RobloxPlayerBeta.exe with the URI, does it get the actual game process PID, or can a launcher chain spawn the real process and exit?
resolved_gaps.answer: Stock handler IS RobloxPlayerBeta.exe (HKCU Software\Classes\roblox-player\shell\open\command; cleanest path is HKCU Software\ROBLOX Corporation\Environments\roblox-player\clientExe), so CreateProcess on it normally yields the client PID directly. EXCEPTION: when an update is required the client chains through <versionDir>\RobloxPlayerInstaller.exe then %TEMP%\Roblox\RobloxPlayerInstaller.exe -relaunch <URI>, so the final game process is a DIFFERENT PID (multi-instance M8/M9 verify, local installer logs). Track clients by (PID, create_time) and re-bind within ~120s via the log's GameJoinLoadTime 'userid:' line; a FOREGROUND/channel-mismatch update closes all RobloxPlayerBeta processes. If the handler is Bloxstrap/Fishstrap, the PID returned is the bootstrapper's, not the client's - detect that and warn.

still_open: Does POST https://auth.roblox.com/v1/authentication-ticket/ still accept an empty or {} body, or is the clientAssertion from GET /v1/client-assertion/ now mandatory? Needs one real-account test; the website falls back to {} when the assertion GET fails, which suggests the empty body still works. Blocks confidence in the launch flow but has a safe default (mirror the site: GET client-assertion, ignore failure, POST with assertion-or-{}).

Does RequestPrivateGame with only placeId+linkCode actually join for an account that NEVER called resolve-link or opened the share link (i.e. can one account's resolved link be reused across alts in a bulk launch)? Needs a real-account test. Safe default: resolve per account with that account's own cookie.

Does an account's OWN cookie, querying its OWN userId via presence, return its own gameId/placeId regardless of its 'who can join me' privacy? Unresolvable without a cookie. Decides whether the 'read account #1's server from presence' fallback for same-server mode is viable; the pre-select-jobId approach avoids needing this.

Is ANY endpoint (especially authentication-ticket) currently ENFORCING x-bound-auth-token (HBA/BAT)? Staff deferred hard enforcement and removed the ASP opt-out (treating it as a background risk signal), but risk-based challenges remain possible. Exact 401 body expected is 9002 subcode 2. Cannot test without a real session; keep per-account WebView2 profiles so the browser's non-extractable HBA key survives as a fallback if enforcement returns.

Are cookie-AUTHENTICATED rate limits counted per-account (session) or per-IP? This decides whether bulk-refreshing N accounts' info from one PC multiplies the budget or shares it. The Data-Stewardship post lists only 'Cookie' vs 'Unauth' rpm with no per-IP/per-account statement. Assume shared-per-IP until proven otherwise.

Does WebView2 CreateCookie with Domain 'roblox.com' (no leading dot) create a host-only cookie that www/apis subdomains do NOT receive? This is the crux of the Tauri injection bug (T3). Needs a dev-build runtime test (no cookie value required, but needs a GUI run, out of scope for this read-only pass). Mitigation is known: always inject '.roblox.com' via raw CookieManager.

Does launching account B (ticket redeem) overwrite the desktop Roblox app's persisted login via the shared RobloxCookies.dat, and does it disturb instances already running under account A? Strongly suggested by the shared-store behaviour but not decrypted/verified; needs a real launch. Drives whether 'shared-login protection' must be on by default.

Auth-ticket lifetime and single-use status, plus the authenticated per-account/per-IP rate limit on authentication-ticket and whether a 429 there carries Retry-After. All require a real session; pace bulk launches conservatively (one at a time, >=~1s spacing, honour x-ratelimit-*) until known.
